s1.syndrome_frame: A firm, fixed mass in the breast with a history of prior breast cancer treatment
salient_findings: Firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
Mammography showing a focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space
Ultrasonography revealing a lobulated, well-defined mass
key_facts: 59-year-old woman
Lump in the lower outer quadrant of her left breast
History of breast-conserving surgery
Endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast
Prior carcinoma in the upper inner quadrant of the left breast
Six years since prior breast cancer treatment
20 mm firm mass on examination
Overlying skin uninvolved
No palpable axillary lymph nodes
Mammography showing a focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space
Ultrasonography revealing a lobulated, well-defined mass measuring 17.5 × 16.4 × 10.6 mm
Core-needle biopsy suggesting atrophic mammary glands
Lesion increased in size on three-month follow-up

shortlist.label: Locoregional breast cancer recurrence
shortlist.why_kept: History of prior breast cancer and new firm mass in the same breast

shortlist.label: Radiation-induced sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of radiation therapy to the breast and new mass in the irradiated field

shortlist.label: Phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Lobulated, well-defined mass on ultrasonography and rapid growth

shortlist.label: Fat necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast-conserving surgery and radiation, and mammography showing a focal asymmetrical density

shortlist.label: Sarcoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: New firm mass in the breast with a history of prior breast cancer treatment

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of breast-conserving surgery and radiation to the left breast, and now presents with a new lump in a different quadrant of the same breast, which has increased in size on follow-up, suggesting a possible recurrence of breast cancer.

rejected.label: Radiation-induced sarcoma
rejected.why: While possible, radiation-induced sarcoma is a rare complication and the time frame of six years since radiation therapy is relatively short for this condition.

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: The description of the mass does not specifically suggest the characteristic features of a phyllodes tumor, such as rapid growth or a large size at presentation.

rejected.label: Fat necrosis
rejected.why: The clinical and imaging findings, including the firm mass and its location in the retromammary space, do not strongly support fat necrosis, which typically presents with more characteristic mammographic and ultrasonographic features.

rejected.label: Sarcoma of the breast
rejected.why: Primary sarcomas of the breast are rare and the presentation in this case, with a history of breast cancer and radiation, makes locoregional recurrence a more likely explanation for the findings.
